newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower on moderate volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower on moderate volumes.

text.p: New York precious metals futures end lower Monday on moderate volumes as the complex continued to drift back from the three-week highs seen last week.

"Interestingly, the choppy trade recently has raised gold's historic volatility a bit, and gold equities rallied nearly 14 percent before drifting back in the last day or two, so gold may be putting in a base around current levels," Chase Manhattan managing director, Dinsa Mehta said.
COMEX December gold ended down $1.40 an ounce at $379.70, after trading in a $381.50-379.40 range.
Spot gold in the bullion market closed quoted $378.80/379.30, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $379.10 and the New York close Friday around $380.05/380.55.
"Gold remains rangebound with $385 basis spot as the top end of the trading range, while $378 seems to be the bottom for the time being," Merill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said.

With both December gold and silver due to enter the delivery period on November 27, short covering by funds and rolling of positions into forward months, may also keep gold rangebound and keep pressure on the contangos, traders said.
The December 1996/February 1997 spread narrowed by a further 20 cents Monday to $1.70 an ounce.

Open interest in COMEX gold rose Friday by 2,672 lots, after falling sharply last week. While December gold is still the most active contract, February gold saw the largest rise in open interest Friday, gaining 1,414 lots.
Bearish fundamentals factors continue to dominate though, analysts said.

CRU International estimates imports into Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Dubai and Turkey has fallen some 15 percent in the first nine-months this year compared to the same period last year, with the strength of the U.S. dollar seen as the underlying cause for the drop in consumption.

Meanwhile, year-end forward sales by producers have been noted and are likely to continue, analysts said, with the price of gold topping out in terms of the South African rand, after seeing multi-year highs around 1800 rand in late October.
COMEX December silver closed down 5.5 cents at $4.883 an ounce, after trading in a $4.940-4.870 range.
While some support for spot silver has developed around $4.85 an ounce, the long term downtrend since February remains intact, providing resistance on any rebound toward $5.00, analysts said.
The December 1996/March 1997 spread has also widened to 7.2 cents Monday from a low of 6.6 cents on November 6, analysts noted.
The spot gold/silver ratio slipped further to 76.93 by the close Monday, but remains within its long term uptrend since May.
"The ratio is expected to remain in favor of gold over the longer term, with 80-85 the objective," Smith Barney analyst Phil Tiger said.
NYMEX January platinum closed down 60 cents at $389.00 an ounce, while the April platinum/April gold spread widened $1.00 to $7.80 an ounce, continuing its recovery from a low of zero on October 25.
NYMEX December palladium closed down $1.40 at $119.25 an ounce early.
-- Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1640; email: clive.mckeef@reuter.com
